verdict.rationale: Appwrite's docs say databases run on a shared pool Appwrite manages, or on dedicated compute provisioned per project. They describe managed database APIs with permissions and realtime, and say developers can use its many SDKs or the REST/GraphQL APIs, with the CLI able to generate a type-safe SDK from the database schema. The specific split between client SDK and server SDK reads/writes is implied rather than explicitly documented. missing for 10: explicit documentation of row read/write through both client and server SDKs, independent hands-on corroboration of SDK database access

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision a managed database and read/write it from client and server SDKs

citations.quote: An Appwrite database runs either on a shared pool that Appwrite manages for you, or on compute provisioned for your project alone.
Choose the database that fits your use case, from managed APIs with permissions and realtime to dedicated native engines you connect to directly.
You can use one of our many SDKs or integrate directly through the REST API or GraphQL API.
The generate command creates a type-safe SDK tailored to your project. It detects your project's language and generates typed helpers based on your database schema.
